author: smimon
text:
As my understanding is developing, I'm beginning to see that price reactions can usually be anticipated in advance equally as much by drawing zones from ignored FTRs that we've momo'd over, as opposed to precise SR flip locations.

Before, I was fixated on drawing very exact SR lines, and then trying to pinpoint the immediate supply or demand level to the left that caused the engulf, or was an FTR formed from the engulf.

My odds of spotting higher strength higher probability reversal zones have gone up greatly when I go up a couple of TFs, and draw in the actual supply or demand zone at the top/base of the ignored FTR, rather than just using a precise line.

An example would probably be helpful.

I hope I've managed to articulate myself properly!

Edit: typo on chart image - "Must better reaction" should be "Much better reaction"

author: smimon
text:
Not wanting to jinx it, but the ACAD trade is proceeding well for now. My tighter stop entry got taken out by just a few pips, but my wider stop entry held.

I set a second limit within H1 supply after the engulf of the FL that was my original target. I revised the target after my initial limit order got activated after a RT from this level - I reasoned that after 2TB, there wasn't much demand left, and the level broke.

I'm now looking lower to the source of the strong move up. Although this in itself was created from the engulf of a FL, and a reaction to ignored supply, so I wonder if this will also get broken - bearing in mind the strong daily demand level we took out way down at the base of the whole up move.

There was a very strong up move from my new target level, and if my 2 trades reach this level, it'll be about 30% on the account, and I'm happy to take it, without getting greedy. I'll monitor any RT from my target level, and if it looks like it's faltering at a good place, I'll get on again looking for more downside.

author: smimon
text:
Not updated in a few days, just still in a position of some frustration. My lack of patience is killing my account. I know the score - HTF zone, wait for LTF engulf, trade the RT to source or QM level, but I'm still trying to be a smartass too often and "pick" tops or bottoms.

author: smimon
text:
Not posting any charts up at present, just using this as a place to air my thoughts, so bear with me;-)

I've regressed this week, quite badly. Last week I added over 50% to my account on 2 separate days, finishing the week in total with triple what I started it with. This week I've completely blown the demo account back to zero. Have I suddenly lost the ability to trade? Nothing quite so dramatic I'm sure.

I got utterly destroyed by a trending day on JPY today. I expected most JPY pairs to continue lower to more significant demand, and so I was just looking short all day on most of them, as supply level after supply level just got wiped out. It's my own fault for not waiting for LTF engs to show me the way, but I'd been taking some really good TTs off levels recently. If I had just known "trade long only" at the start of the day... But then that's the skill required. One of my biggest weaknesses remains when I get my "short goggles" on, and I'm determined to try and short something at any opportunity, despite what PA is telling me.

I know I'm not far off - I wasn't making the trades I was making by chance. but I simply must learn to recognise who is in control at any given point, buyers or sellers. When I get this right, I trade very well. When I get it wrong, it's a total farce.

Rome wasn't built in a day, etc etc, but I'm particularly bad at dealing with frustration. And when you don't have patience, and a calm objective eye in this game, you're in all sorts of trouble.

Some days I feel ready to go live with my real cash, and others it still feels a million miles away until I've achieved that sort of consistency.

Got a nice 4 day break coming up over the weekend and a couple more days for my birthday, so hopefully the time off will do me some good and allow me to come back refreshed and refocused.

My hats off to all those on here who are consistently profitable and who can read the charts so well.

All the best

author: smimon
text:
Just a couple of hours away from the charts, came back, reassessed everything, saw exactly what I'm doing wrong, the trades I should have taken screaming at me, I feel the mojo is back already. Once you've achieved a certain level, it becomes a reference point for you - even if you fall short, you know what you are capable of, and that it's surely just a matter of time before you get back to where you were.

Just to prove I've not lost the plot, and to reinforce the methodology in my head by rote, a quick analysis of a CJ continuation trade that was painfully obvious today. From now on (and this is what I was doing last week), I want to see something basing at the HTF zone for at least an hour or two before I'll try and trade it. There are of course plenty of times that things just spike into levels, and run away - but I don't care about letting those ones go, because they're inherently very risky. When you wait patiently for the basing opportunities, that's when you can get obscenely tight stops with the high RR I crave.

CJ H1 as it stood this morning. We're moving up strongly from D1 demand at the bottom, the last upward surge engulfed an FTR to the left, creating a tidy area of demand as it went. What's the obvious play? Wait for RT to demand, look for continuation. (the red zones at the top are the next important H4/D1 supply zones - I note there is a nice looking hook level at the area where they overlap, I'll keep an eye on that one).

Dropping to M5, this is how price reacted upon RT to the demand zone.

How it played out

Today was a trending day for sure, but they do happen, and this was an easy one to be on the right side of. Time to get my act back together!

Chart is EUR/USD D1.

(in other type of FTR trade where only demand or supply needs to be engulfed I have quite hard time defining this S/D whether it`s good or bad to create FTR) 3. Decision point(FL?) to engulf 1 up. First pole before retracement of this DP did not go above FTR1 so not sure I can call it FL so I call it DP. 4.This DBR faked DP 3 and move continued above high of second pole of DP 3. So I think FTR was created. This FTR-demand is really what holds this flag up - bounces starting with point five etc... From my observation this No.4 FTR can either fake, bounce from or not even touch DP 3 and it would still be FTR. 7. On picture No.2 DP 7 to break FTR4 is created with big move from it and low of this move point 8 also engulfs DP 6 from picture 1. But how to identify that DP 7 will hold for FTB? Only the big move from and engulf of 6 is enough to touch trade it? 9. FTR which is also FTb to DP 7 is created and will be confirmed when it breaks 8?

So this is my understanding, now I am going to read all your journal posts since you have much better understanding of things as I see from some of them

author: smimon
text:
Still alive

Nothing much to report recently, the concepts are gelling in my mind, I realised that I was trading with an incomplete set of principles - namely CP and FOs. I know I've been saying this for a while, but I really do feel on the cusp of everything fitting together big time.

I'll post some trades up when I feel like I'm in a position to be completely thorough in my analysis, and when I'm winning consistently. The type of thing like I did for the EU analysis above.

I've got a plan also, which requires me to be more consistent. As soon as I get into profit for the day, I'm considering it "free money". My money is my starting capital for the day, anything else is the market's money, which I'm borrowing. This is to be used aggressively. I trade with 4% risk currently. I'm looking for small scalps initially, 2R or so (or whatever the reading of the chart tells me is available). If I win 8%, I will stake it all on my next trade. If that one wins, I will do it once more. Essentially a 3 trade accumulator. If I lose, I'm back to my starting capital for the day, and I reduce my risk back to normal and start again.

2 or 3R compounded 3 times off an initial 4% risk for the day equals a very healthy daily addition to the account. Also, it'll hopefully stop me going for unrealistic targets.

author: smimon
text:
Hey pal. I'm not sure I've heard of the concept of trading inside the flag?

Remember, price is essentially the same on all timeframes, in terms of CP, FTR, S/D levels, engs etc. It just all happens a lot quicker on LTF. Apply exactly the same concepts that you would to analyse HTF on LTF to pinpoint precise entries from HTF zones.

If I know the HTF zone we are reacting to is a significant one, and it's in the direction of the D1/W1 trend, then I will sit and monitor LTF for a good opportunity to get into that move, by looking for an eng from the zone, and then looking for some CP RT back up to a good level. If the D1/W1 trend is down, we've reacted short with an eng off the HTF zone, and then I can see a CP move back up to a good supply level - I'll take that all day long.

I trade off HTF zones in the sense that I wait for LTF reaction from them, and then use that as my directional bias to enter a trade in what is most likely to be the correct direction.

Not sure if this answers?

author: smimon
text:
So yesterday I was a bit rusty after being away from the charts for a while, and made 6 losses in a row. Normally at this point, I'd get enraged at my demo account, and start manically trying to get it all back by putting stupid sized trades on. However, I kept my cool, and actually won it all back in a series of measured, calculated trades.

Since I felt like my consistency was improving, after my first trade won today, I decided to roll over the profits as planned into my next.

First trade:

I made about 14% off 4% risk on this one, so decided to roll 10% into my next trade -free cash, market's money, don't get attached to it etc - it's just there to drive profit aggressively. Just protect your own capital, what you start the day with.

Second trade - setup on M5 was a reaction to a FL formed after the break of a SR level, zone shown.

The trade itself, M1:

Combined with the 14% from the first trade, this put me at a total of about 47% account gain for the day, off 2 trades. I think I like this method.

AU ripped up much higher after my target. This was foreseeable - the initial "top" which I was targeting off M1 was formed at a DBD level, there being a much better RBD level above which capped price. I could have taken half off at my first target, and let the rest run, and still been up handsomely on the day even if it didn't work out. However, the lot size was pretty big (for me) on the 2nd trade, and a single giant pin from my target level would have wiped out 1/3 of my profit.

Probably better to enter the trade in 2 separate parts - I'll code something up to let me do this. Still, only the first day trying this technique, so can't be too dismayed.

author: smimon
text:
I'm waffling a little here, but it's my journal so I have license;-)

I realise that I've moved somewhat away from HTF analysis of late, and am focusing more on scalps, rather than looking for trades I can hold over a period of a day. My entries are from HTF, but my targets are not. This just seems to suit my mentality - I'm quite an impatient person, and I like to see results from my trades quickly. I'm of course aware that I'm missing out on some much greater opportunities to run my profits, so hopefully when I've got more experience, I can combine the power of getting these very accurate M1 entries with some sound HTF analysis, and get into the realms of these 20R+ trades that I know are possible.

At present, if I try to analyse and trade from HTF only, if I'm wrong, it takes me several hours to find out, and then I have to wait several hours more for the next chance to trade. I'm going to continue to do what's working for me, but make sure to check out the long term road map for situations where I can go for the big results. AU this morning was a good example - I took less than half of what I should have held for, but I got a bit giddy because I had 10% of rolled over profit on it.

Different strokes for different folks!
